items.title: IND (1784): Foundation of the Asiatic Society of Bengal (Calcutta)
items.meta: Sir William Jones (under Governor-General Warren Hastings)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Foundation of the Asiatic Society of Bengal (Calcutta)

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Sir William Jones (under Governor-General Warren Hastings)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Established Orientalist scholarship in India; Sir William Jones translated Kalidasa's 'Abhijnanashakuntalam' (Sacontalá, 1789) and Jayadeva's 'Gita Govinda' into English, and proposed the Indo-European language family hypothesis (1786).

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Marks the peak of the Orientalist phase of British rule prior to the Anglicist shift.

items.title: IND (1792): Charles Grant's 'Observations on the State of Society among the Asiatic Subjects of Great Britain'

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Charles Grant's 'Observations on the State of Society among the Asiatic Subjects of Great Britain'

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Charles Grant (Clapham Sect Evangelicals)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: First systematic evangelical tract advocating the introduction of the English language and Christian Western education in India; laid the ideological groundwork for the Charter Act of 1813.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Charles Grant is frequently called the 'Father of Modern Education in India' in pre-1813 colonial policy questions.

items.title: IND-02 (1794): The Travels of Dean Mahomet

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: The Travels of Dean Mahomet

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Sake Dean Mahomed

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Published in Cork (Ireland) in 1794 in epistolary form; first book ever published in English by an Indian author.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Must-know chronological anchor for Unit VI and Indian Writing in English.

items.title: IND (1800): Establishment of Fort William College, Calcutta
items.meta: Lord Wellesley (with John Gilchrist & William Carey)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Establishment of Fort William College, Calcutta

fields.label: Key Person / Body

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Founded to train British East India Company civil servants in Indian languages, laws, and administration; catalyzed modern prose printing and grammars in Bengali, Urdu, and Hindi.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Tested alongside the 1817 Hindu College (founded by David Hare, Raja Rammohun Roy, and Radhakanta Deb).

items.title: IND-03 (1813): Charter Act of 1813 (East India Company Act — Rs 1 Lakh Grant)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: colonial_act_or_minute

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: British Parliament

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Ended Company trade monopoly (except tea/China), permitted Christian missionaries, and allocated Rs 1 lakh annually for 'the revival and improvement of literature' and science in India.

items.title: IND-04 (1817): Foundation of Hindu College

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Foundation of Hindu College

fields.label: Key Person / Body

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Established 20 January 1817 to provide secular Western and English education to Indian youth; Henry Louis Vivian Derozio taught here (1826–1831).

items.title: IND-05 (1823): Raja Rammohun Roy's Letter to Lord Amherst on Western Education

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Raja Rammohun Roy's Letter to Lord Amherst on Western Education

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Raja Rammohun Roy

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Written 11 December 1823 protesting the establishment of a government Sanskrit College in Calcutta and pleading for instruction in European natural philosophy, chemistry, mathematics, and anatomy.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Repeatedly asked in UGC NET for who wrote the letter, to whom (Lord Amherst), and in what year (1823).

items.title: IND-06 (1835): Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education & Bentinck's English Education Act
items.meta: Thomas Babington Macaulay & Lord William Bentinck

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education & Bentinck's English Education Act

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Thomas Babington Macaulay & Lord William Bentinck

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Minute dated 2 February 1835; endorsed by Bentinck on 7 March 1835. Advocated 'Downward Filtration Theory' to create 'a class of persons, Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect'.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Single highest-yield institutional topic in Unit VI. Know exact dates (2 Feb & 7 March 1835), quotes ('a single shelf of a good European library'), and Governor-General (Bentinck).

items.title: IND-07 (1854): Wood's Despatch on Education ('Magna Carta of English Education in India')
items.meta: Sir Charles Wood (President of the Board of Control) to Lord Dalhousie

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Wood's Despatch on Education ('Magna Carta of English Education in India')

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Sir Charles Wood (President of the Board of Control) to Lord Dalhousie

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Issued July 1854. Rejected rapid downward filtration alone; recommended vernacular primary schools, Anglo-vernacular high schools, grants-in-aid, female education, teacher training, and universities at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras on the London University model.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'; led directly to the establishment of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras Universities in 1857.

items.title: IND (1857): Establishment of the Universities of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Establishment of the Universities of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Lord Canning (implementing Wood's Despatch of 1854)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Created the first three modern affiliating and examining universities in India modeled on the University of London, formalizing English Literature and language examinations at the BA/MA level.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Note the sequence: Calcutta (Jan 1857), Bombay (July 1857), Madras (Sept 1857); Punjab University (1882) and Allahabad University (1887) followed later.

items.title: IND-08 (1882): Indian Education Commission (Hunter Commission)
items.meta: Sir William Wilson Hunter (appointed by Lord Ripon)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Indian Education Commission (Hunter Commission)

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Sir William Wilson Hunter (appointed by Lord Ripon)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Reviewed progress since Wood's Despatch (1854); emphasized primary education through vernaculars and divided secondary education into literary (for university entry) and vocational/commercial streams.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: First major post-1857 education commission; often paired in chronological ordering questions with 1854, 1902, and 1917.

items.title: IND-09 (1902): Indian Universities Commission (Raleigh Commission) & Universities Act 1904

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Indian Universities Commission (Raleigh Commission) & Universities Act 1904

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Sir Thomas Raleigh & Lord Curzon

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Appointed in 1902 by Lord Curzon, leading to the Indian Universities Act of 1904; tightened government control over university senates and emphasized postgraduate teaching/research.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Frequently tested in chronological sequence of colonial commissions (1854 -> 1882 -> 1902 -> 1917).

items.title: IND-10 (1917): Calcutta University Commission (Sadler Commission, 1917–19)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Calcutta University Commission (Sadler Commission, 1917–19)

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: education_commission

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Sir Michael Sadler

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Recommended separating Intermediate (10+2) education from university degree courses (creating the 3-year Honours degree structure) and stressed mother-tongue instruction at secondary level alongside English.

items.title: IND-11 (1948): University Education Commission (Radhakrishnan Commission, 1948–49)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: University Education Commission (Radhakrishnan Commission, 1948–49)

fields.label: Key Person / Body

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: First commission on higher education in independent India; recommended replacing English gradually with an Indian language as medium, while retaining English as a vital 'window on the world' and library language; led to UGC formation (1953/1956).

items.title: IND-14 (1964): Indian Education Commission (Kothari Commission, 1964–66)

fields.value: Report titled 'Education and National Development' (1966); formalized the 'Three-Language Formula' (National Policy on Education 1968) and defined English as an essential 'library language' in higher education.

items.title: IND (1968): First National Policy on Education (NPE 1968) — Three-Language Formula

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: First National Policy on Education (NPE 1968) — Three-Language Formula

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Government of India (Indira Gandhi Administration)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Officially implemented the Kothari Commission's Three-Language Formula across Indian states, cementing English as a compulsory modern language and 'window on the world' in secondary and higher education.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Distinguish NPE 1968 (Three-Language Formula), NPE 1986 (Navodaya Vidyalayas, IGNOU/Open University), and NEP 2020 (5+3+3+4 structure & mother-tongue instruction).

items.title: IND-15 (1981): Study Group on the Teaching of English (Gokak Committee Report)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Examined ELT syllabus design, remedial English, and bridging the gap between literature departments and communicative language skills in Indian colleges.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Links Indian English poetry/criticism (V.K. Gokak) with institutional ELT policy.

items.title: IND-16 (1989): Masks of Conquest: Literary Study and British Rule in India

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: Masks of Conquest: Literary Study and British Rule in India

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Gauri Viswanathan

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Landmark postcolonial institutional study arguing that the academic discipline of 'English Literature' was institutionalized in colonial India (1820s–1830s) as an instrument of moral/political control BEFORE it was established in English universities.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: One of the most frequently asked critical books across Unit VI, Unit VII, and Unit IX.

fields.label: Key Person / Body

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Argues that colonial contact caused 'cultural amnesia' disconnecting modern Indian criticism from classical Sanskrit (*marga*) and vernacular (*desi* / *bhasha*) traditions.

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: Extremely high-yield text bridging Unit VI (English in India) and Unit VIII (Indian Criticism).

items.title: IND (2020): National Education Policy (NEP 2020)
items.meta: Dr. K. Kasturirangan Committee (Ministry of Education)

fields.label: Commission / Act / Milestone Title
fields.value: National Education Policy (NEP 2020)

fields.label: Key Person / Body
fields.value: Dr. K. Kasturirangan Committee (Ministry of Education)

fields.label: Core Provisions
fields.value: Replaced the 10+2 system with the 5+3+3+4 curricular structure; emphasized mother-tongue/regional language medium up to at least Grade 5 (preferably Grade 8), multidisciplinary 4-year undergraduate degrees, Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), and translation via the Indian Institute of Translation and Interpretation (IITI).

fields.label: UGC NET Exam Significance
fields.value: High-yield contemporary policy milestone for Unit VI and Paper I Higher Education.
